 IOWA — Applications are open for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program or LIHEAP, and HACAP is urging eligible households to apply early because funding is not guaranteed through the end of the season.
 LIHEAP provides eligible households with a credit on their utility bills to help with heating costs. HACAP administers the federally funded program across east central Iowa, serving communities from Dubuque to Cedar Rapids and Iowa City.
 "If you think about how cold the winters get in Iowa, it's really nice for people to have that peace of mind that they can not get shut off during the the winter time and still keep their heat," Christopher Ackman, HACAP’s communications manager, said.
 LIHEAP assistance in the past year
 HACAP processed 10,456 applications in the past year, with 9,249 households approved. The agency provided $4.31 million in assistance, and the average award was $486.51.
 Ackman said the help can leave households with more room in their budgets for other expenses.
 “You think about food assistance, you think about gas, you think about the rising cost of groceries. This is just one thing that can hopefully help people's budget at the end of the month," Ackman said.
 How to apply
 Household income must be at or below the poverty guidelines to qualify. Applications can be submitted online or in person. HACAP asks applicants to provide a recent utility bill and Social Security cards for everyone in the household.
 Applicants usually hear back in about 30 days. The deadline to apply is April 30, but HACAP encourages applicants to apply as soon as possible.
 "We really want people to apply before it gets really cold outside, that's the main thing," Ackman said. "Since it's a heating assistance program, we want to make sure that people are getting in as early as possible."
